mark_customer: Hey — during yesterday's migration we started seeing a large spike of 429/503 and some customers reported duplicate charges. Looks like retries from the Python SDK are re-sending without preserving idempotency header. Sharing logs below.

mark_customer: ```
2026-02-20T15:02:10.123Z INFO request id=req_ABC attempt=1 status=502 idempotency=abc-123
2026-02-20T15:02:10.234Z INFO backoff sleep=0.120 jitter=0.000 seed=42
2026-02-20T15:02:10.355Z INFO request id=req_ABC attempt=2 status=502 idempotency= -
2026-02-20T15:02:10.477Z INFO backoff sleep=0.120 jitter=0.000 seed=42
2026-02-20T15:02:10.598Z INFO request id=req_ABC attempt=3 status=503 idempotency= -
```

mark_customer: minimal repro below, using python-sdk 0.8.6

mark_customer: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="redacted", retries=3, backoff_base=0.12, jitter=True)
resp = client.create_charge(customer_id="c_123", amount=100)  # no explicit idempotency_key
```

anna_support: thanks for the report — can you confirm the SDK version and whether you're running sync or asyncio? also any `x-request-id` values from our logs would help. :eyes:

mark_customer: sdk=0.8.6 (pypi), sync mode, sample x-request-id values above are `req_ABC`

anna_support: grabbing eng. @dave_engineer do we have any known regressions around idempotency header preservation + retries in 0.8.6?

ci-bot: deploy 0.8.7 -> staging finished at 2026-02-21T08:12:03Z :white_check_mark:

dave_engineer: hi — thanks, this looks familiar. there's a bug in 0.8.6 where the idempotency header can be dropped on connection-reuse retries in the requests/AioHTTP adapter. the jitter seeding logic also had a corner-case that made jitter deterministic when the backoff base is small and connection is reused. both fixed in 0.8.7.

lucy_sre: symptoms match: repeated attempts logged with identical `seed` and `jitter=0.000`, idempotency header blank on attempts >1. that can cause a server to process a retry as a fresh create.

dave_engineer: repro steps we used: run a loop of 100 create_charge calls with a flaky proxy that returns 502 on the first attempt, confirm 2nd/3rd attempts in client logs lack `Idempotency-Key`. the fix ensures header is copied onto the retry request and reseeds jitter per-attempt.

anna_support: recommended short-term workarounds:
- upgrade to `redwood-sdk==0.8.7` (preferred)
- or set `retries=0` and implement your own retry loop that preserves an explicit `idempotency_key` (e.g., `str(uuid4())`)
- or set `client.default_idempotency_key = lambda: str(uuid4())` before calls

mark_customer: can you share the pip upgrade command and what to watch for in logs after?

dave_engineer: `pip install -U redwood-sdk==0.8.7`
After upgrade, enable debug logs: `export REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1` and look for per-request lines like:
```
INFO request id=req_ABC attempt=2 idempotency=abc-123 jitter=0.085 seed=137
```
You should see idempotency preserved on attempts >1 and non-zero jitter values.

mark_customer: ok running upgrade now on staging. will report back in ~30m. :thumbsup:

mark_customer: quick follow-up — can't upgrade yet in prod, any immediate mitigation?

dave_engineer: set `retries=0` for Prod and add explicit header in your request call: `client.create_charge(..., idempotency_key=str(uuid4()))`. That will avoid duplicate processing even if a retry happens outside the SDK.

mark_customer: deployed `retries=0` + explicit idempotency_key to prod. monitoring.

mark_customer: update after 2 hours — no new duplicate charges, 429/503 still show intermittently but no duplicates. will schedule SDK upgrade next week. thanks all. :relieved:

anna_support: great. we'll keep the 0.8.7 release notes and link in the ticket. reopening if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
